fix(d-187): the truncation clause reduces in whole steps and advises a budget that covers the gap

Two renderings of the same clause were wrong in the collapsed run status.

PR #17's own review printed `… `budget-usd` $1.15 would ` -- the 160-character
bound was applied as a slice, so the sentence stopped inside the word that
carries the advice. The block now reduces in the same three whole steps the
line above it already used (D-190): the whole clause, else the `budget-usd`
sentence alone, else nothing. Both surfaces extract that sentence from one
shared pattern.

PR #15's own review printed `$0.0010 short; `budget-usd` $1.00 would have read
it` with `budget-usd` already at $1.00: the needed figure was rounded to the
nearest cent and landed on the setting in force. The quoted figure is now
rounded up to the cent, so it always covers the gap; the exact figure stays
in the exception and in the ledger.

REDs first in tests/test_status.py and tests/test_budget_ledger.py. No
constant moved.
